document.title: Osama bin Laden: Taliban Spokesman Seeks New Proposal for Resolving bin Laden Problem (State 220495)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] After the Taliban Supreme Court finds insufficient evidence against bin Laden, Wakil Ahmed tells DCM Alan Eastham that Kandahar does not consider the matter resolved and that Saudi Arabia holds the key. Eastham corrects Wakil's claim that bin Laden was U.S.-supported, saying the U.S. had never heard his name in that period. Wakil also says Saddam Hussein was the root cause of the problems. Excised.

mentions.quote: THE FIRST WAS AN UNAUTHORIZED NEWS CONFERENCE IN KHOST AND THE STATEMENT HE HAD MADE FOLLOWING THE AIRSTRIKES

events.description: Eastham and POLCOUNS met Wakil Ahmed at the Taliban 'ambassador's' residence for 90 minutes; Wakil sought a new US proposal on bin Laden.
US cruise missile attack on Afghanistan; Wakil says 22 Afghans killed and 55 wounded.
East Africa embassy bombings.
Taliban Supreme Court ruled insufficient evidence against bin Laden.
US Charge Eastham meets Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed in Islamabad; Wakil proposes joint Saudi-Taliban ulema delegation to resolve the bin Laden issue.
Wakil returns to Kandahar to meet Pakistani delegation of MFA and ISI representatives on bin Laden.
US temporarily closes embassy in Bangkok and issues threat warning for Vienna over bin Laden threat intelligence.
Charge Eastham, with the political counselor, met Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed at the Taliban 'ambassador's' residence; Wakil sought a new US proposal on bin Laden and urged no more bombing.
US cruise missile attack on Afghanistan; Wakil claimed 22 Afghans killed and 55 wounded.
East Africa embassy bombings brought bin Laden's presence in Afghanistan to the forefront; Eastham had worked at the Nairobi embassy.
Taliban Supreme Court ruled that no evidence warranted the conviction of bin Laden.
Cable Islamabad 008803 transmitted to State as State 220495, reporting the Wakil meeting.
East Africa embassy bombings, attributed by US to bin Laden's network.
US cruise missile airstrikes on Afghanistan after the bombings; bin Laden issued statement afterward.
Bin Laden held an unauthorized news conference in Khost.
Taliban Supreme Court decision on bin Laden disappointed the US.
Wakil Ahmed met US Charge in Islamabad (cable date) to discuss resolving the bin Laden problem.
Planned Clinton–Nawaz Sharif talks in Washington on bin Laden (the Wednesday after the cable).
US temporarily closed its embassy in Bangkok and issued threat warning on Vienna due to bin Laden intelligence.
Wakil to return to Kandahar to meet Pakistani MFA/ISI delegation on bin Laden.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is harbored in Afghanistan by the Taliban.
relationships.quote: THE PRICE THE TALIBAN WERE PAYING, AND WOULD CONTINUE TO PAY, FOR HARBORING BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Senior Taliban spokesman.
relationships.quote: SENIOR TALIBAN SPOKESMAN WAKIL AHMED

relationships.detail: Meeting in Islamabad on 28 Nov 1998.
relationships.quote: CHARGE (ACCOMPANIED BY POLCOUNS) MET WITH WAKIL AHMED EARLY ON SATURDAY MORNING

relationships.detail: Earlier discussions with Ambassador Milam on bin Laden.
relationships.quote: HE HAD EARLIER ASKED AMBASSADOR MILAM WHAT WOULD HAPPEN IF BIN LADEN WERE TURNED OVER

relationships.detail: Taliban proposed joint Saudi-Afghan ulema meeting to resolve bin Laden issue.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD GIVEN THE SAUDIS AN AUTHENTIC PROPOSAL FOR RESOLVING THE BIN LADEN ISSUE

relationships.detail: Wakil to meet Pakistani delegation from MFA and ISI in Kandahar.
relationships.quote: REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND ISI

relationships.detail: Implied leader whose view on bin Laden matters.
relationships.quote: THE PROBLEM OF MULLAH OMAR'S VIEW.

relationships.detail: Wakil speaks as Taliban spokesman, conveying Taliban positions on the bin Laden issue.
relationships.quote: WAKIL SAID THAT THE TALIBAN WOULD ALSO BE DISCUSSING BIN LADEN WITH THE PAKISTANIS.

relationships.detail: Wakil believes the Saudis hold the key to resolving the bin Laden problem and hopes they will talk to Kandahar again.
relationships.quote: WAKIL SAID HE BELIEVED THAT THE SAUDIS HELD THE KEY TO RESOLVING THE PROBLEM.

relationships.detail: Joint Saudi-Taliban ulema proposal; Saudis asked the Taliban to bind bin Laden's hands and deliver him.
relationships.quote: THEY SIMPLY WANTED THE TALIBAN TO BIND THE HANDS OF BIN LADEN AND DELIVER HIM OVER.

relationships.detail: A Pakistani delegation including MFA representatives was to meet Taliban in Kandahar.
relationships.quote: MEET WITH A PAKISTANI DELEGATION (WHO HE LATER SAID WOULD CONSIST OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND ISI)

relationships.detail: ISI representatives were part of the Pakistani delegation to meet Taliban in Kandahar.
relationships.quote: REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND ISI

relationships.detail: Wakil met the US Charge in Islamabad to discuss bin Laden.
relationships.quote: CHARGE REITERATED THAT THE U.S. CONTINUED TO INSIST THAT BIN LADEN BE EXPELLED

relationships.detail: Wakil was returning to Kandahar to meet the Pakistani delegation.
relationships.quote: HE WAS RETURNING TO KANDAHAR TODAY

relationships.detail: Taliban harbor bin Laden and pay a diplomatic, economic and military price for it.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WERE PAYING, AND WOULD CONTINUE TO PAY, FOR HARBORING BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: US Charge says bin Laden and his network remain active and in touch with his people.
relationships.quote: BIN LADEN AND HIS NETWORK WERE STILL ACTIVE

relationships.detail: Taliban Supreme Court decision on bin Laden did not resolve the matter in Taliban view.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN DID NOT CONSIDER THE BIN LADEN MATTER RESOLVED IN THE WAKE OF THE RECENT SUPREME COURT DECISION

relationships.detail: Mullah Omar's view is a factor in Taliban handling of bin Laden.
relationships.quote: HE MAY BE TRYING TO DEAL WITH THE PROBLEM OF MULLAH OMAR'S VIEW.

relationships.detail: Eastham is the US Charge reporting to Washington.
relationships.quote: CHARGE PROMISED TO REPORT BACK TO WASHINGTON ON THEIR CONVERSATION

relationships.detail: Charge based in Islamabad where Wakil visited.
relationships.quote: ASKED WAKIL IF HE HAD PLANS TO RETURN TO ISLAMABAD

relationships.detail: Wakil called Saddam Hussein the root cause of all these problems.
relationships.quote: SADDAM HUSSEIN WAS THE ROOT CAUSE OF ALL THESE PROBLEMS

relationships.detail: Albright signed as Secretary of State.
relationships.quote: UNQUOTE: ALBRIGHT

relationships.detail: Wakil Ahmed is described as a senior Taliban spokesman.
relationships.quote: SENIOR TALIBAN SPOKESMAN WAKIL AHMED TOLD CHARGE THAT KANDAHAR DID NOT BELIEVE THAT THE BIN LADEN MATTER HAD BEEN RESOLVED

relationships.detail: Eastham previously worked three years at the US Embassy in Nairobi and lost friends in the bombing.
relationships.quote: HE HAD PREVIOUSLY WORKED FOR THREE YEARS AT THE U.S. EMBASSY IN NAIROBI AND HAD LOST MANY AMERICAN AND KENYAN FRIENDS IN THE BOMBING

relationships.detail: Wakil earlier told Ambassador Milam that a terrorist can become a hero and vice versa.
relationships.quote: HE HAD EARLIER TOLD AMBASSADOR MILAM THAT SOMETIMES A TERRORIST BECOMES A HERO AND SOMETIMES A HERO CAN BECOME A TERRORIST

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is present on Afghan soil.
relationships.quote: THE PRESENCE OF OSAMA BIN LADEN ON AFGHAN SOIL TO THE FOREFRONT

relationships.detail: The Taliban Supreme Court is the Taliban judicial body that ruled on bin Laden.
relationships.quote: THE SUPREME COURT HAD RULED THAT THE NO EVIDENCE HAD BEEN PRESENTED WHICH WARRANTED THE CONVICTION OF BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: The court ruled that insufficient evidence was submitted to implicate bin Laden in terrorism.
relationships.quote: RECENT TALIBAN COURT RULING THAT INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE HAD BEEN SUBMITTED IMPLICATING BIN LADEN IN TERRORIST ACTIVITIES

relationships.detail: A joint Taliban-Saudi ulema proposal was earlier made on bin Laden; relations are now in deep freeze.
relationships.quote: THE EARLIER JOINT. TALIBAN-SAUDI ULEMA PROPOSAL COULD STILL PROVIDE THE COVER THE TALIBAN LEADERSHIP NEEDED TO PART WAYS WITH BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Taliban-Riyadh relations are awkward and in a deep freeze over the bin Laden issue.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN RELATIONS WITH RIYADH HAD BECOME AWKWARD RECENTLY DUE TO THE BIN LADEN ISSUE

relationships.detail: Wakil sought a new US proposal for resolving the bin Laden problem and discussed a US-Taliban agenda on narcotics, human rights and terrorism.
relationships.quote: ASKED INSTEAD FOR A NEW U.S. PROPOSAL AIMED AT RESOLVING THE MATTER

relationships.detail: The Taliban were under pressure from the UN, among others, to expel bin Laden; a Russian-proposed UNSC resolution would invalidate Taliban passports.
relationships.quote: RECENT RUSSIAN-PROPOSED UNSC RESOLUTION, WHICH PROPOSED TO INVALIDATE TALIBAN-ISSUED PASSPORTS

relationships.detail: Wakil claimed bin Laden had once been a trained guerrilla supported by the US; the Charge denied US support for him.
relationships.quote: BIN LADEN HAD ONCE BEEN A TRAINED GUERILLA SUPPORTED BY THE UNITED STATES

relationships.detail: Wakil alleged the US gave asylum to General Malik.
relationships.quote: GIVING. "ASYLUM" TO GENERAL MALIK, WHO HAD BEEN RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEATHS OF FIVE THOUSAND AFGHANS

relationships.detail: The US met with Pakistani political leader Khan Abdul Wali Khan, cited by Wakil as an anti-Taliban initiative.
relationships.quote: MEETING WITH (PAKISTANI POLITICAL LEADER) KHAN ABDUL WALI KHAN

relationships.detail: The Charge acknowledged US meetings with General Malik as routine contact with Afghans.
relationships.quote: WITH RESPECT TO MEETING WITH WALI KHAN AND GENERAL MALIK AND REPORTS OF U.S. "DELEGATION"

relationships.detail: A US delegation reportedly visited the Panshir Valley, an anti-Taliban area.
relationships.quote: SENDING A U.S. DELEGATION INTO THE PANSHIR VALLEY

relationships.detail: The US viewed bin Laden as the person who provided leadership and guidance to those who carried out the East Africa bombings.
relationships.quote: BIN LADEN WAS THE PERSON WHO GAVE LEADERSHIP AND GUIDANCE TO THE PEOPLE WHO HAD DONE THIS

relationships.detail: Taliban leadership is referred to as Kandahar.
relationships.quote: KANDAHAR DID NOT BELIEVE THAT THE BIN LADEN MATTER HAD BEEN RESOLVED

relationships.detail: Wakil asks the US Charge for a proposal to resolve the bin Laden problem.
relationships.quote: HE ASKED CHARGE FOR A USEFUL PROPOSAL FROM THE U.S. THAT WOULD SERVE TO FINALLY RESOLVE THE PROBLEM.

relationships.detail: Charge thanked Wakil for his presentation and discussed prior talks in Kandahar and Islamabad.
relationships.quote: CHARGE THANKED WAKIL FOR HIS PRESENTATION

relationships.detail: Taliban Supreme Court decision seemed to change Taliban from host to protector and collaborator of bin Laden (direction: Osama is recipient, Taliban provider).
relationships.quote: CHANGE THE STATUS OF THE TALIBAN FROM HIS HOST TO HIS PROTECTOR AND COLLABORATOR.

relationships.detail: US officials' meetings with Wali Khan and General Malik were cited by Taliban as suspected conspiracy; Charge denied it.
relationships.quote: WITH RESPECT TO MEETING WITH WALI KHAN AND GENERAL MALIK AND REPORTS OF U.S. "DELEGATION".

relationships.detail: Bin Laden held an unauthorized news conference in Khost.
relationships.quote: AN UNAUTHORIZED NEWS CONFERENCE IN KHOST

relationships.detail: Taliban imposed a prohibition on bin Laden speaking out and warned he would be prosecuted for sponsoring terrorism.
relationships.quote: THESE VIOLATED THE TALIBAN-IMPOSED PROHIBITION ON HIS SPEAKING OUT.

relationships.detail: Charge asked whether Taliban had spoken again to Prince Turki after the Saudi Interior Minister's statement.
relationships.quote: WHETHER THE TALIBAN HAD SPOKEN AGAIN TO PRINCE TURKI BIN FAISAL

relationships.detail: Wakil had earlier asked Ambassador Milam what would happen if bin Laden were handed to the US.
relationships.quote: WAKIL SAID HE HAD EARLIER ASKED AMBASSADOR MILAM WHAT WOULD HAPPEN IF BIN LADEN WERE TURNED OVER

relationships.detail: Wakil says the Saudis seized most of bin Laden's wealth.
relationships.quote: THE REST HAD BEEN SEIZED BY THE SAUDIS.

relationships.detail: Wakil says Saudis would pay more for handover of bin Laden than bin Laden himself could give.
relationships.quote: THE SAUDIS WOULD GIVE THEM A LOT MORE FOR TURNING OVER BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Clinton was to talk with Sharif in Washington about bin Laden and seek his help.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT CLINTON WOULD BE TALKING TO PAKISTANI PRIME MINISTER NAWAZ SHARIF ABOUT BIN LADEN ON WEDNESDAY IN WASHINGTON

relationships.detail: Wakil returning to Kandahar to meet Pakistani delegation of MFA and ISI representatives.
relationships.quote: MEET WITH A PAKISTANI DELEGATION (WHO HE LATER SAID WOULD CONSIST OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND ISI)

relationships.detail: ISI representatives to meet Wakil in Kandahar on bin Laden.
relationships.quote: REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND ISI

relationships.detail: Taliban leadership in Kandahar decides on bin Laden's fate.
relationships.quote: THE LEADERSHIP IN KANDAHAR NEEDED TO DEAL WITH.

key_claims: Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed said expelling bin Laden without compelling proof or religious cover would cause the Taliban's fall.
Wakil asked the US for a new proposal and urged no more cruise missile strikes.
Wakil said Saudi Arabia held the key via the joint Saudi-Taliban ulema proposal.
US Charge insisted bin Laden must be expelled to a place where he could be tried, and warned of further strikes.
Taliban Supreme Court ruled there was no evidence to convict bin Laden.
US analysts suspected internal Taliban disagreements, possibly involving Mullah Omar's view.
Taliban said Pakistan was under pressure; a Pakistani MFA/ISI delegation was to visit Kandahar.
